description: The line plot illustrates the harmfulness of responses, measured as the "Harmful with Refusal Ratio," across different models and datasets as a function of the number of training steps, with the x-axis representing the number of steps on a logarithmic scale ranging from approximately 128 to 1024. The y-axis, also on a logarithmic scale, ranges from 0.1 to 0.5, indicating the ratio of harmful responses that were refused. Four distinct models are compared: LlaVA-1.5-7B on FigStep (blue line with circles), Qwen2-VL-7B on FigStep (orange line with squares), LlaVA-1.5-7B on MMSafetyBench (green line with triangles), and Qwen2-VL-7B on MMSafetyBench (red line with diamonds). All four lines show an increasing trend in harmfulness with more training steps. At 128 steps, the harmfulness ratios are approximately 0.23 for LlaVA-1.5-7B on FigStep, 0.18 for Qwen2-VL-7B on FigStep, 0.1 for LlaVA-1.5-7B on MMSafetyBench, and 0.27 for Qwen2-VL-7B on MMSafetyBench. By 1024 steps, the ratios increase to approximately 0.5 for Qwen2-VL-7B on MMSafetyBench, 0.48 for Qwen2-VL-7B on FigStep, 0.47 for LlaVA-1.5-7B on FigStep, and 0.45 for LlaVA-1.5-7B on MMSafetyBench. The Qwen2-VL-7B model on MMSafetyBench consistently exhibits the highest harmfulness ratio across all training steps, while LlaVA-1.5-7B on MMSafetyBench shows the lowest.
